name: cosmo
tagline: A PostgreSQL flight deck for your terminal
description: cosmo is a terminal user interface that provides real-time visibility into PostgreSQL database health, query performance, lock contention, and WAL/MVCC internals — a flight deck for your database without leaving the shell. It connects directly to your Postgres database and gives a live view of everything: active queries, WAL throughput, connection health, lock contention, cache efficiency, and table bloat, all updating in real time. No browser, no external service, no configuration beyond a database URL. It queries Postgres system views directly — pg_stat_activity, pg_stat_database, pg_stat_checkpointer, and pg_locks — and calculates WAL rate by tracking the change in WAL LSN between refreshes. A four-panel layout covers database vitals, workload, WAL and MVCC, and locks and waits, with a compact single-panel mode, keyboard navigation, and an animated mission-control boot sequence. Built in Go with Bubbletea, Lipgloss, and pgx.
highlights: Live database vitals, workload, WAL, MVCC, cache, connections, and lock contention
Connects with just a database URL — no browser, no external service
Queries Postgres system views directly, with WAL rate computed from LSN deltas
Four-panel flight deck plus compact single-panel layout and keyboard navigation
Real-time view of active queries with duration, and lock waits with wait events
curatorNote: A lightweight real-time Postgres monitor from the terminal — low-friction alternative to heavy GUI monitors, surfaced on r/commandline at just 53 stars. For anyone who lives in a terminal and runs Postgres, this is the kind of tool that makes you look at your database differently.
